races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: Hold-up 7yo for the 3lb claimer Conor Stone-Walsh; fades in the finish according to flags, and a sim-going record of 12/15 with zero wins at this course distance combination makes it hard to construct a winning case here.
runners_data.comment: Aurora Nova has run over today's trip and, rated 63 against an official mark of 54, there is a case she is better than her recent winless sequence suggests; the risk is that six starts without troubling the judge makes the turnaround hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: 4yo hold-up type with headgear noted; W J Lee is an upgrade in the saddle and the sim-going record shows two wins from 15 attempts, though a drop from 8f to 6f is a question, and recent form at this trip (two 13ths) is deeply concerning.
runners_data.comment: Blue Anthem steps into this from stall two carrying 143 lb, and his experience over today's trip counts in his favour alongside a third last time out that shows he is not far off this level; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Devil's Angel
runners_data.note: Veteran 10yo whose natural style is hold-up — this race's volume of closers means the horse is pushed toward midfield on the map but is not a natural racer from there; 88 days off the track and a modest OR of 49 compound the risks, though a 4th at Standside 6f on soft is a positive trip marker.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 88 days off, Devil's Angel faces questions about both form and fitness, though he has run over today's trip before and our rating of 60 suggests more ability than his official mark of 49 implies.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Hold-up 8yo that has raced exclusively at 7f-8f in recent history and is trained by Mulvany, who is 2/20 in the last 14 days; running back after just 8 days, the drop to 6f looks sharp and the sim-going form at this trip distance is thin (13/15).
runners_data.comment: Dinamine has managed just one win in his last six starts, finishing unplaced in each of his two most recent outings, and our figures rank him tenth of twelve here, making him difficult to fancy; he has run over today's trip before and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround, but that may be the best that can be said.

runners_data.name: Distillate
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's 6yo comes back after 8 days with a truly poor sim-going record (6/15, one placed); pushed into midfield on the map because the hold-up ranks are overcrowded, so the horse faces a positional challenge that suits it poorly, and a DNF in recent form is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Distillate at least has experience of today's trip and a solid speed rating of 67 to suggest ability, though an unplaced effort eight days ago and a run disrupted by a brought-down incident cloud her chance from stall 5 off 143 lb.

runners_data.name: Goldrush Kid
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 5yo returning after 152 days off, which is the longest absence in the field; headgear fitted, Patrick Magee sends out rarely-successful runners (1/9 in 14 days), and the step down from 16f to 6f is extreme — best treated with deep suspicion.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Goldrush Kid does at least have experience over today's trip and our rating of 71 puts him clear of his rivals, though 152 days off the track is a significant unknown ahead of this return.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: McGuinness's 4yo prominent runner is the most recent winner in the field (1st, 8f, good) and retains the same trainer who is in form (4/30); the drop to 6f from his winning trip is the key concern, but his prominent style lets him race without traffic issues.
runners_data.comment: Land Of The Giants advertises strong recent form with a win last time out, and at just eight days since that success he returns quickly; has run over today's trip before, and our rating ranks him second of twelve, though the patchy earlier form in the book is the worry.

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, also from the McGuinness yard (in-form at 4/30); STYLE_FIT flag means her natural distance is longer (won at 10f twice recently) and 6f may find her out for pace, so the front-running role is genuinely uncharted — James Ryan's experience is the saving grace.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts back, She's Ideal arrives on a quick turnaround of nine days and has run over today's trip, but that eighth last time out tempers enthusiasm, and 143 lb from stall 12 adds further to her task.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Eagles
runners_data.note: Colin Keane — the most decorated jockey in this field — rides a hold-up 6yo who has won over 6f on good going in his last five; the horse's sim-going profile (7/15, 1 win) is moderate but the jockey-horse match at this trip is the strongest tactical argument in the race.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise when third four starts back and a winner five starts back, Spirit Of Eagles has disappointed in her last three outings, all eighth or sixth; experience over today's trip and 34 days of freshening offer slim hope from stall nine off a mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: 5yo hold-up type whose last five runs are all at 8f-12f, making 6f a very significant trip shortening; Cian Hughes sends him back after just 8 days and the redistribution to midfield compounds an already awkward positional ask — form at sprint trips is untested.
runners_data.comment: Thompson Gunner has finished fifth in two of his last three starts and, though he won a start back in his recent form, he has looked well held on current figures and is ranked ninth of twelve here; experience over today's trip offers little comfort when the overall profile makes him difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: 4yo rated just 46 with no listed jockey, a fade-in-finish flag, and a last run of only one day ago — the fastest turnaround in the field; sim-going record (8/13) is moderate, and the horse is a genuine hold-up type who ends up mapped to midfield because the closers' ranks are full, reducing any late-run chance further.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of these on our figures, Heart Of Eternity also has a trainer who has gone 0/23 in the last 14 days; having run just yesterday, this filly faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Cordouan
runners_data.note: 8yo veteran with a fade-in-finish flag and OR of just 41 — the lowest-rated runner; 14 days since last run is fine, but recent form figures of 8-0900 over 8f are grim, and the horse's natural late-run style is blunted by being squeezed into the midfield mapping zone.
runners_data.comment: Cordouan has been winless in his last five starts, failing to reach the frame on four of those occasions, and ranked eleventh of twelve on our figures he faces a stiff task here; experience over today's trip is about the best that can be said in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: She's Ideal is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field at 6f on turf, and with no genuine rival likely to push her early, she should stride into a comfortable lead and set a controlled, even gallop rather than a pressure-cooked tempo. Land Of The Giants and Goldrush Kid are the other prominent types who will track close but neither carries the profile to burn She's Ideal off the front, meaning the pace is unlikely to collapse the field into a heap. This shape — a sustainable, uncontested lead — historically favours hold-up horses who can produce one sustained run when the field compresses in the final two furlongs, and with Colin Keane aboard Spirit Of Eagles and a deep pool of closers, the late-running profile is genuinely live. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can place cleanly at the rear: Distillate, Devil's Angel, Thompson Gunner, Heart Of Eternity and Cordouan are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, with Spirit Of Eagles and Blue Anthem the most likely to secure the natural back-marker positions given their distance/speed profiles at this trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Charge
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the field strings out behind, leaving room for hold-up horses to pick off tiring rivals late.
scenarios.body: She's Ideal sets a sustainable tempo that flatters neither herself nor the prominent pair, and the final furlong becomes a sprint for the closers as she runs out of petrol; Spirit Of Eagles, with Colin Keane's positional judgement, and Blue Anthem are ideally suited to swoop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal's recent course-winning form translates and the hold-up brigade are bottled up in traffic in a pack-heavy field.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up types forced into midfield, the pack gets congested and no horse gets a clean passage, allowing She's Ideal to steal enough of a margin that it holds; Land Of The Giants, tracking close in second, picks up the pieces if She's Ideal fades.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Long Shot
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield creates interference and the race splits into chaotic groups leaving a gap for an overlooked hold-up runner to thread through.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of five genuine hold-up horses into the midfield zone creates a compressed, messy middle section, and a horse like Spirit Of Eagles or Devil's Angel who finds daylight late benefits most from the resulting scramble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Goldrush Kid and Land Of The Giants press She's Ideal harder than expected, turning the race into a war of attrition that burns out the field behind.
scenarios.body: An end-to-end gallop would suit a horse who can race prominently and stay grinding, and Land Of The Giants — who won over 8f on good ground recently — has the stamina to outstay rivals as the pace-pressure takes its toll on She's Ideal.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Of Eagles is in the hands of Colin Keane — if he gets a clean passage from mid-rear in the final 2f, the horse's proven 6f good-ground form makes it a serious threat to all.

She's Ideal carries a STYLE_FIT flag (natural trip 10f+) — watch whether James Ryan allows her to stride clear early or is forced to restrain, as either choice creates a different race shape entirely.

The McGuinness yard saddles three runners (She's Ideal, Land Of The Giants, Distillate) — stable instructions between them will shape the early tempo and whether Land Of The Giants is ridden to press or to track.
Goldrush Kid's 152-day absence and the dramatic distance drop from 16f to 6f makes it a significant drifter risk in the market — any unexpected market move for this runner should be noted pre-race.
Heart Of Eternity ran just one day ago — watch the market and paddock closely for any signs of distress or flat coat, as a turnaround of 24 hours into a 12-runner sprint is highly unusual.

races.name: Gilna's Of Laytown Handicap

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer on good ground with one win and two places in similar going from his history — best run was a second over 8f, and dropping to 6f is a concern; however the short eight-day turnaround for McGuinness is a warm trainer angle to monitor.|
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and returning on a quick eight-day turnaround, Moyassr arrives in good nick and has run over today's trip, while his speed rating of 67 gives him a strong look against this field; the main risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Volendam
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; Gainford can dictate but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) notes this is slightly out of role, and a 38-day absence for a lightly-campaigned yard (T14: 0/3) tempers confidence — he has limited turf wins in similar going and could be vulnerable if the pace stretches him.|
runners_data.comment: Second two starts back and a winner six starts back, Volendam has shown ability in recent starts but the unplaced effort last time and a weight of 154 lb are checks on enthusiasm; she has run over today's trip and returns after 38 days off.

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent form — won over 7f on good ground 16 days ago for the in-form Cian Hughes/Colin Keane combination (T14: 1/7); steps back to 6f but has placed over the trip and looks the most dangerous horse if sitting second on a controlled pace.|
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and a winner three starts back, Launch Time arrives here in decent nick after just 16 days, but his speed rating of 72 and a ranking of ninth of thirteen suggest he faces a stiff task, and the seventh two starts back is a concern.

runners_data.name: Verhoyen
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up type who has run four times on good ground without a win and just two places; 92-day absence and age make this a tough assignment even if he settles into a comfortable rear position.|
runners_data.comment: Verhoyen shaped with promise when fourth three starts back and steps up on an official mark of 52, with our rating of 63 suggesting he is well treated; winless in his last five starts and returning after 92 days, though the distance experience and stall one make him an interesting profile here.

runners_data.name: Ukiyo
runners_data.comment: Ukiyo has run over today's trip before and shaped with promise when second and third in recent starts, but she has been winless in her last six outings and a sixth last time out suggests she may need things to fall right from stall nine carrying 144 lb.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a second and a third from recent starts on good ground, mapped to midfield only because the rear is overcrowded; STYLE_FIT (0.92) flags the positional compromise — if he can't settle as he would naturally, his closing kick may arrive too late.|
runners_data.comment: Jazzit arrives here 21 days fresh, with a second and a third in recent starts offering encouragement, though he is winless in his last six and that latest unplaced effort is a concern; he has run over today's trip and carries 142 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Colugo
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up type mapped to midfield due to redistribution; STYLE_FIT (0.91) and a 69-day layoff are concerns, and his recent turf form shows no wins or places in the past five — needs everything to fall perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Colugo faces a stiff task, though three thirds in recent form and experience over today's trip offer slim crumbs of comfort after 69 days off.

runners_data.name: Akashaa
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been consistently placed — second and third in career — but those placed efforts came on Standard going at Dundalk; the drop to 6f on turf good marks a significant profile change, and racing out of natural position adds further doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of sixth-place finishes her most familiar calling card, Akashaa is hard to fancy from stall 12 off 138 lb, and our figures rank her near the foot of this field, though she does have experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Inishmot Prince
runners_data.note: See above — note consolidated above.|
runners_data.comment: Inishmot Prince shaped with promise when winning four starts back, and he has run over today's trip, giving him an obvious fitness edge in terms of experience; the main risk is a lengthy 174-day absence since he last appeared.

runners_data.name: Star Allure
runners_data.note: No wins or places in the last five and a sim-going score of just 3/15 on good turf — one of the horses with the least appealing profile for today's conditions; redistributed from rear to midfield, compounding the positional mismatch.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with three unplaced efforts among her four most recent outings, Star Allure faces a stiff task ranked bottom of the field on our figures, though she has run over today's trip before and returns after a 38-day break.

runners_data.name: Hot To Foxtrot
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose true style has been pushed into a midfield map position by the volume of closers in this field; has four placed efforts on good ground over sprint trips and the 38-day break is not a concern, but racing out of role is a meaningful discount.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Hot To Foxtrot does at least bring distance experience and a return from a 38-day break that could see her sharper, though an unplaced effort last time and an official mark of 50 suggest she faces a stiff task from stall four carrying 144 lb.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: Prominent type without a declared jockey listed, which demands monitoring; has five recent runs on good ground, won over 5f on good going and placed twice, making him a legitimate pace presence if he gets his position cleanly over this 6f trip.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Platino Bianco has finished unplaced or fifth-or-worse in four of her last five starts, with only a win five starts back offering any encouragement; experience over today's trip and a 19-day break count for little given the overall profile.

runners_data.name: Are You In Or Out
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with three career wins on good ground and 6f form — recent form includes a win and a runner-up finish in similar conditions; 19 days since last run is fine but the absence of a listed jockey is worth noting before committing.|
runners_data.comment: Are You In Or Out showed a winner in her last five starts, with that success coming five starts back, and she has run over today's trip, arrives fit at 19 days since her last run, and draws stall 2 carrying 150 lb; the risk is that her more recent outings have been unplaced.

races.paceDynamic: Volendam is the only confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine pace rival likely to contest the lead, Jordan Gainford should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Laytown's straight six furlongs. The bulk of the remaining runners — Moyassr, Jazzit, Colugo, Akashaa, Inishmot Prince, Star Allure and Hot To Foxtrot — are true hold-up types, but so many of them are present that several will inevitably be pushed forward into unnatural midfield positions rather than settling at the rear. Launch Time and Platino Bianco are the most credible prominent challengers who may actually secure an early position behind Volendam, with Hot To Foxtrot and Jazzit the redistributed hold-up horses most likely to end up tracking the pace rather than coming from off it. A single front-runner setting a measured tempo on flat, straight Laytown turf creates the classic scenario where prominent racers travelling just off the pace hold the decisive positional advantage — the race shape strongly favours horses who can sit second or third early and pounce without having to make a wide, sweeping run from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Volendam Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Volendam secures the lead uncontested and sets a fair but not punishing gallop, the race is run to suit horses tracking just behind.
scenarios.body: Gainford controls tempo from the front and the prominent runners behind — particularly Launch Time — get a soft lead to hunt down in the final furlong; a steady gallop on flat Laytown turf means those who race prominently but still have a gear-change hold the edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Overrun Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses push forward and crowd Volendam, creating a more contested early pace that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A busier early pace on the flat Laytown straight causes Volendam to fold once the early rush is absorbed, benefiting those who have settled just off the messy early pace and quicken late; Launch Time, who has the tactical speed and recent winning form over 7f in good going, is ideally suited to exploiting a moderate competitor that has run itself into the ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late-Closers Arrive Unmolested
scenarios.trigger: If Volendam goes so slowly that energy is conserved all the way to the two-furlong pole, compressing the field and allowing hold-up horses an unusually easy closing run.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling pace negates Volendam's advantage and allows genuine hold-up horses like Moyassr and Are You In Or Out — who has three career wins in this going on 6f — to produce a late rattle that catches the leaders flat-footed; this scenario is less likely given the number of runners likely to be pushed wide of their natural position, muddying the late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Off The Beach
scenarios.trigger: If the unique Laytown conditions — tidal surface variations, awkward starting stalls behaviour or a wide draw — disrupt early running positions and scramble the field.
scenarios.body: Unpredictable early order unsettles Volendam's pace-controlling role and hands the advantage to versatile or lightly-weighted types who can adapt; Platino Bianco, who has course-surface experience on good ground and has been placed from a prominent position, could capitalise on positional scrambling.

watchPoints.text: Volendam holds the pace key — watch whether Jordan Gainford can maintain a comfortable lead from the gate; if he is immediately crowded by redistributed hold-up horses like Hot To Foxtrot or Jazzit pushing forward against their natural style, the tempo could spike and unwind his advantage entirely.

Launch Time is the prime beneficiary if Volendam goes easy — watch Colin Keane's positioning in the first furlong; if he slots directly onto Volendam's quarters, this horse has the form and the jockey to win from that position.

Are You In Or Out and Platino Bianco both lack a declared jockey in the data — confirm riding arrangements before the off, as a last-minute jockey change can affect tactical instructions and early positioning.

The Laytown going is listed as unknown across all reports — any surface softening caused by tidal activity near the track could shift the balance toward horses with soft-ground entries in their history, notably Volendam (placed on Soft) and Launch Time.

Trainer T G McCourt runs two horses (Jazzit and Inishmot Prince) — watch for any stable market move that might indicate which is the yard's primary hope, as both are hold-up types displaced from their natural position in this race shape.

races.name: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Collective Power
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Edward Lynam who has run 6f on good ground twice in recent history without threatening; trainer in 0/2 form over 14 days and sim-going record is a modest 6/15, but its style suits the dominant scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Collective Power appeals as the top-rated runner in this field and shaped with promise when third two starts back, giving him strong claims despite carrying 168 lb from stall 11; the main concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Recent winner (1/7f good) and trainer Andrew Slattery flying at 7/24 over 14 days; however its last five runs are all at 7f-8f, and dropping to 6f as a confirmed front-runner into a pace battle of its own making is a significant stamina question — the pace war may consume it.|
runners_data.comment: Faoladh won last time out and his trainer is firing at 29% in the past fortnight, but two unplaced efforts in the three starts prior to that win and 40 days off the track give pause; he has run over today's trip and carries 168 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Initial Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with excellent 6f turf form (three recent placed efforts at the trip on standard going) and a winning mark at the distance; dropped in class here and has H C Swan in the saddle, though 70 days off the track is worth noting on first run back.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down on our figures among these thirteen, Initial Blue has been off for 70 days and the weight of 168 lb is a stiff ask, though he does show a win last time out and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Sporting Hero
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose sim-going record shows only 4/15 runs on comparable ground; won over 5f on good for Durkan 14 days ago but the step back to 6f in a pace-heavy race asks whether it can get involved late having been beaten in double figures in its most recent 6f starts.|
runners_data.comment: Sporting Hero brings a recent win in his last six starts to recommend him, and he has run over today's trip before; the concern is that his last four outings have yielded three unplaced finishes and a sixth, so he must bounce back sharply from that patchy recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Profit Surge
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a solid recent record (1W, 6P on good) and back quickly after just 9 days; its natural desire to lead puts it at the heart of the pace controversy — it will press hard early and the question is whether Ian Donoghue's runner has enough left when Faoladh and Minaun View refuse to yield.|
runners_data.comment: Profit Surge won two starts back and has placed on four other recent occasions, so she clearly knows how to compete, and she has run over today's trip before; however, fourth last time out on a quick nine-day turnaround and a hefty 166 lb to carry may test her reserves here.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner, trained by Adrian McGuinness (4/30 over 14 days) and raced 9 days ago; all five recent runs are at 7f-10f on good, so this step back to 6f is a sharp trip drop — its jumping-off instincts may have it press the pace but lack of 6f form is a red flag.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Minaun View has finished fifth in each of her last two starts and looks hard to fancy here, though she does own a win three starts back and has run over today's trip, arriving fit on a nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Una Matata
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from the same McGuinness yard as Minaun View, also returning after 9 days; all recent form is at 7f-8f and sim-going record is thin at 3/15, so the 6f trip on a fast-pace day looks stretched for a horse that has finished out of the frame in five of its last six.|
runners_data.comment: Ran sixth last time out and has been largely out of the frame in recent starts, though she did score one start further back — a win six starts back — and has run over today's trip before; the 165 lb burden from stall 8 makes life harder.

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse by style but the crowded rear means it is unlikely to get its preferred position — its actual back-marker role is undermined here; trainer Slattery is in strong 14-day form (7/24) but Kitty Bear's six most recent runs show it hasn't won beyond 6f and its best recent placing came at 8f.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with only one win in her last six starts, Kitty Bear is a tough proposition, though she has run over today's trip before and a trainer striking at 29% in the past fortnight offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: This horse is a genuine closer whose last-to-first profile (1/6f good in recent form) is compelling, but with three confirmed pace horses dictating the shape, it will be shuffled closer to midfield than it wants to be, blunting its finishing punch; hg:t noted and Paul Flynn is 0/16 over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Rappell has won once in his last six starts, with that victory two starts back and a second three starts back offering some encouragement, but an unplaced return latest and a lowly ranking on our figures make him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: Consistent short-course performer with four of its last five runs at 5f-6f on good and placed in several; by nature a hold-up type, though forced into a more forward-facing map position given pace congestion — its best form on this going (12/15 sim-going runs) still shows it as competitive when getting its run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Bold Optimist at least showed a flash of promise with a third and a second earlier in that sequence, though consecutive unplaced efforts since are a concern; he has run over today's trip and returns quickly on eight days' rest carrying 162 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 72 and an Edwardy Lynam-trained hold-up specialist with strong 6f good-ground credentials (3/6f good, 1/6f good in recent history) and hg:t; last ran just 1 day ago which is a significant fitness query that must be respected before drawing conclusions.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back, Jon Riggens arrives here just one day after his latest run which may test his stamina for the contest, but he has experience over today's trip and a 9 lb pull on his official mark gives him a solid profile to build on.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: Another OR 72 hold-up type from the McGuinness yard, also back after just 8 days; all five recent runs at 7f-8f suggest this 6f trip on a testing pace day is sharper than ideal, though hg:t, placed form on good (2/8f, 3/8f) and a 0W5P recent run string suggests consistency without the final decisive kick.|
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced profile but No More Porter showed enough when third two starts back to merit respect here, and his 76 rating edges above his official mark of 72 — drawing stall four carrying 171 lb is the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from Claire O'Connell's yard, returning after 9 days; form figures suggest inconsistency (two wins but also several tail-end finishes) and recent runs at 7f-8f on good haven't been convincing — 6f in a strongly-run race is a tough ask for a horse whose sim-going record shows 8/15 exposure but no recent hints of recapturing form.|
runners_data.comment: Gloriously Glam is winless in her last six starts, though a second three starts back hints at ability; a 9-day turnaround keeps her fresh, but 159 lb from stall 13 makes life harder for a filly rated 60 on her official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh, Profit Surge, and Minaun View are all confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field over 6f at Laytown, and with all three likely to press for early supremacy, a strong, honest gallop from the outset is virtually guaranteed. The pace battle between these three will stretch the field early, burning fuel on the stands side and ensuring the race is run as a genuine test of stamina rather than a sprint-finish dash. Hold-up horses Rappell, Kitty Bear, and Bold Optimist are genuine closers by nature but have been pushed into a midfield representation on the map because the field is already stacked with pace-setters and true back-markers — none of those three will comfortably get their natural position off the pace, diluting their closing threat. This race shape firmly favours hold-up runners who can settle just off the carnage and produce a sustained run in the final two furlongs — Jon Riggens, No More Porter, and Collective Power are the profile types best suited to sit and pounce once the pace battle unravels.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Them
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh, Profit Surge, and Minaun View fight for the lead and set a genuinely punishing gallop that exhausts the front three inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will see the lead group tie up before the line, opening a clear late lane for horses who have settled off the speed; genuine hold-up types that have been able to sit and conserve energy become the primary beneficiaries. Jon Riggens and No More Porter, both with strong 6f form on good ground and the profile to close fast, are ideally positioned to mop up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Faoladh given recent winning form — establishes a clear lead early while the others fade or are outpaced from the break.
scenarios.body: Faoladh's recent win form and strong good-ground record (13/15 sim-going runs showing experience) would allow it to set a measured rather than suicidal pace, preserving enough to hold on late. Prominent types travelling comfortably just behind the leader — Initial Blue and Una Matata — would be best placed to peg back any leader that slows without burning out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Pays
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves moderately strong but not extreme, compressing the field and allowing midfield runners to time their runs without being caught too far back.
scenarios.body: A compact field with no extreme attrition would allow horses like Rappell and Bold Optimist — genuinely held-up types forced to run from midfield — to produce their finishing kick from a slightly more forward position than they'd prefer, increasing their chance; Sporting Hero with its previous 5f win on good ground could also pick off fading rivals. The catch is that neither Rappell nor Bold Optimist are racing in their natural role, which limits the conviction of this shape even if it materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If two of the three front-runners miss the break or are checked early, leaving a single leader to dictate a falsely run race at a much steadier gallop.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace over 6f would compress the field and turn the race into a late sprint, benefiting sharp prominent types who save all their energy — Initial Blue and Gloriously Glam, both with placed form on good ground, would stay competitive deep into the race under this shape. Hold-up horses would be caught flat-footed with nowhere to come from, and Faoladh's stamina-biased profile would be less effective without a true test.

watchPoints.text: Jon Riggens ran just 1 day ago — watch for any official declaration confirmation and signs of fatigue in the paddock; if fit and well, the 6f good-ground profile and hold-up style is tailor-made for this pace scenario but the turnaround is unusually sharp.

Faoladh, Profit Surge, and Minaun View are on a collision course for the lead — watch the first two furlongs closely to see if one capitulates early or if all three burn against each other, as this directly determines whether Scenario A or Scenario B plays out.

Rappell's last win came over 6f on good ground and it has the form to be dangerous, but watch whether Miss A B O'Connor can get it covered up in the early stages — if the redistribution forces it wide and prominent, its closing run will be wasted.

Minaun View's trip drop from its recent 7f-10f form base to 6f in a hot pace makes it vulnerable to folding inside the final furlong; watch how quickly P W Mullins sends it forward and whether it retains any energy past halfway.

Initial Blue has been off 70 days — watch its paddock demeanour and early racing behaviour for signs it is ready first time back; a fresh, well-schooled prominent racer returning over its best trip could easily outrun a long absence.

races.name: Pride Of Place Maiden

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a lone win over 16f on Good ground and two placed efforts in similar conditions; jockey Jack Kearney takes a 3lb claim which helps at the weights, and 15 days since last run is a comfortable prep — needs the pace to set up for a late run.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form is modest but did place twice on Standard-type surfaces; 35 days between runs is borderline fresh, and the 7f trip at Laytown on Good is within range, though he has failed to win from 15 career starts and that record tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Fan Club
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with directly relevant 7f Good turf form, but the 448-day absence for Denis Hogan is a significant fitness query — if he bounces out and leads freely he is dangerous, but a pipe-opener run after this layoff is a realistic outcome.

runners_data.name: Joe Cool
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong trainer-jockey angle through Colin Keane; recent run just nine days ago is short of ideal freshness, and his form has been over middle distances (12-16f), making the 7f trip a genuine question mark despite the high OR of 74.

runners_data.name: Sron Na Caise
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a 2nd place over 8f on Good ground and jockey W.J. Lee providing tactical nous; 58 days since last run and the drop back to 7f from 8-10f trips are both worth noting, but the Good ground record here is directly applicable.

runners_data.name: Tyraxes
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator wearing a tongue tie for the Hogan yard, same trainer as Fan Club — Hogan runs two horses here without a win from 23 starts in 14 days, which tempers confidence; 52 days since last run and form figures suggest he finds a way to be competitive without winning.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has raced prominently in all five recent starts on Good ground and placed four times; jockey Rory Mulligan claims 5lb which aids the weights, and the tongue tie is retained — she will be fighting Fan Club for the early lead and how that battle goes defines her chance.

runners_data.name: Kakori
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Joseph O'Brien whose recent placed form at 10-12f on Good suggests stamina; the step back to 7f is a shortening of trip from his comfort zone, and while Declan McDonogh is an elite rider the horse needs a truly run race to make ground from the back.

runners_data.name: Therewillbeglory
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who is also the trainer-rider, which creates an interesting tactical angle; two 2nd-place finishes on Good ground at 7-8f are directly relevant, and 76 days since last run is the longest gap in the field — a fitness concern, though horses returning fresh have performed here before.

races.paceDynamic: Fan Club and Hugo's Girl are the confirmed front-runners, and with four of nine runners wanting a prominent position — including Joe Cool, Sron Na Caise, Therewillbeglory, and Desert Of The Sea all angling for the early positions — there will be genuine competition for lead and lead-adjacent slots from the jump over Laytown's 7f. Fan Club arrives on a 448-day absence for Denis Hogan and Hugo's Girl has habitually led or raced close-up over shorter trips, meaning neither is certain to dominate cleanly; a contested early pace is the likeliest outcome, with the front pair setting an honest gallop they may not fully control. The prominent cluster creates a meaningful traffic danger between the 2f and 3f poles as the field compresses, and hold-up horses Convincing, Tyraxes, and Kakori will need to navigate wide or find gaps. This race shape — honest pace, congested midrace — tilts the advantage toward hold-up and late-running profiles that can exploit a tiring front rank, particularly those with proven ability on Good turf at similar trips.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fan Club and Hugo's Girl cut out honest fractions and the prominent cluster burns out between 2f-3f, freeing late ground.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace sets up a truly run race over Laytown's 7f, leaving the back markers with a wall of tiring horses to reel in over the final two furlongs; Kakori's recent placed form over 10-12f suggests stamina at this shorter trip, while Convincing's lone win came at 16f but has produced two runs in the places on Good ground at similar class.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Grinds On
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce enough to eliminate Fan Club and Hugo's Girl but one of the prominent quartet conserves enough energy to kick clear.
scenarios.body: Sron Na Caise has place form over 8f on Good ground and jockey W.J. Lee is a strong tactical rider; Therewillbeglory has two 2nd-place finishes on Good ground at 7-8f and trainer Andrew Slattery riding his own horse can set a patient prominent hold from the inside.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Easily
scenarios.trigger: If Fan Club and Hugo's Girl fail to press each other hard and one opens up a clear lead, controlling fractions from the front.
scenarios.body: Fan Club holds the highest OR (69) of the genuine pace types and his form figures at 7f on Good are directly relevant despite the 448-day layoff; if he settles in front without serious pressure he may prove hard to reel in given the modest hold-up quality behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble causes interference or significant traffic issues between the 2f-3f zone and form is thrown out.
scenarios.body: With four prominent types and two confirmed front-runners colliding early, a bunching incident cannot be ruled out entirely; in a messy race the horse with tactical flexibility and an experienced jockey — Joe Cool under Colin Keane — has the profile to emerge from trouble, though Desert Of The Sea's recent placed form also offers each-way interest at a big price.

watchPoints.text: Fan Club and Hugo's Girl will meet head-to-head from the first strides — watch whether either blinks early, as whoever buckles first disrupts the entire pace picture for the race.

The four-runner prominent cluster (Joe Cool, Sron Na Caise, Therewillbeglory, Desert Of The Sea) creates a specific traffic pinch-point at the 2f-3f pole — horses on the inner risk being squeezed and punters should watch Kakori and Convincing for where they are forced to travel.
Fan Club's 448-day absence is the biggest fitness wildcard in the race — if he blows up having led, the race becomes a scrabble for the hold-up horses rather than a controlled late surge.
Joe Cool ran just nine days ago and drops from 14f to 7f — if he fails to settle in the prominent group with Keane, the short turnaround and trip drop could see him fade badly in the final furlong.

Therewillbeglory is trainer-ridden and returns after 76 days — watch his position out of the gates as Andrew Slattery will have a very specific tactical plan, and any significant early move for position could signal he is spot-on after the break.

races.name: O'NEILLS.COM Handicap

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (two wins from last four starts), handles good ground well per sim-going record of 10/15, and drops back to 7f from winning runs over further — hold-up style suits this patient shape and she is the most in-form runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Reponse Finale won last time out and was second two starts back, which reads well on recent form, but our rating of 43 — ranked eleventh of thirteen — flags her as a significant outsider, and a trainer strike rate of 0/39 in the last 14 days makes her hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Veteran of ten at this trip on good ground but sim-going returns 0W1P from 15 starts, suggesting consistency rather than a winning threat; likely to press Marambo and could nick a minor placing if the pace suits a prominent stalker.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of thirteen on our ratings and carrying 150 lb from stall nine, Brains has run over today's trip and returns after a sharp 21-day break looking sharper than his recent finishes suggest — the concern is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Marambo
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with a STYLE_FIT of 0.94, meaning she is effectively being asked to lead despite recent form figures of 10-12-13 — poor recent efforts undermine confidence, but uncontested pace control gives her tactical relevance she does not earn on merit alone.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Marambo nonetheless showed some ability with a fourth and fifth in recent efforts, though three subsequent unplaced runs temper expectations; he has run over today's trip and returns after a sharp 14-day break carrying 150 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is an upgrade in the saddle, but this horse carries a fade-in-finish flag and a sim-going return of 10/15 with zero wins; best placed midfield but difficult to trust in the closing stages over 7f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Lohengrin makes little appeal despite the return to a familiar trip; his sole spark of encouragement is a third last time out, part of a gradually improving profile.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose natural rear position is compressed to midfield here given the volume of backmarkers; all five recent starts have been over shorter trips of 5-6f, raising questions about whether 7f suits, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, I'm Spartacus does at least return quickly on 12 days' rest and has run over today's trip, though a fourth four starts back is the closest he has come to threatening, and the weight of 144 lb from stall 12 gives him little obvious help.

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer shuffled into a midfield mapping — best runs have come on AW and soft variants, with a sim-going return of just 4/15 on turf/good, making Laytown's conditions a real concern for his chances.
runners_data.comment: Roman Harry brings strong claims on our rating despite being winless in his last six starts — a second last time out shows he is running into form, and he has experience over today's trip. Carrying 144 lb from stall 11 is the key weight concern.

runners_data.name: Movin And Groovin
runners_data.note: Won last time at 8f on AW, but turf good-ground sim-going reads 3/15, a significant worry on this surface; pushed into midfield from his natural hold-up berth, and the STYLE_FIT caveat tempers expectations even if his AW form looks eye-catching.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Movin And Groovin has shown she can mix form, and she has run over today's trip before; 26 days between runs keeps her fresh, but a mark of 46 and 143 lb from stall seven are the hurdles she must overcome.

runners_data.name: Chavajod
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at eight and carries both a fade-in-finish warning and a STYLE_FIT discount; form figures of 00-007 are poor and recent history features multiple mid-teens finishes, making him very hard to fancy regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with a string of unplaced efforts, Chavajod is hard to fancy on these figures, ranked tenth of thirteen, though he has run over today's trip before and 29 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Saith Seren
runners_data.note: 83-day absence is a notable flag, and all five recent runs have been placed or finishing fifth, suggesting honest but not winning form; true hold-up type displaced to midfield in the map, with a soft-ground profile that could be a concern if Laytown rides quick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 83 days, Saith Seren does have experience over today's trip and her third last time out shows she can threaten the places, though her rating of 50 and fifth-place finishes in between suggest she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Barretstown
runners_data.note: Consistent at finishing mid-pack rather than threatening — form figures 037000 tell the story, and a sim-going return of 3/15 on similar conditions makes him among the least likely to win; naturally held-up, placed to midfield by the map's constraints.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Barretstown faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a workable 26-day break carrying 137 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Amanirenas
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on AW last time out but carries a fade-in-finish flag and returns a sim-going record of 13/15 runs on today's going type, suggesting she genuinely handles this ground well; no jockey listed which is worth monitoring, and the STYLE_FIT note means her hold-up position is the real one, not the mapped midfield slot.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner three starts back but has been unplaced in both runs since, and a ninth two starts back clouds her recent consistency; has run over today's trip and 18 days off should leave her fresh enough, though 141 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Second from last run over 10f on good ground shows she stays well and handles conditions, but recent form of 775025 is patchy; 8-day turnaround is quick and all five recent runs have been over further than today's 7f, making the trip drop a query.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Perfect Judgement at least showed promise with a second two starts back, and he has run over today's trip before, returning on a quick turnaround of eight days — a rating of 59 makes him the one to beat in a field of thirteen.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Best recent figures include two placed efforts at 10f on good ground and a sim-going record of 13/15 — very comfortable with today's conditions; however, all recent placed efforts have come over a longer trip and the step down to 7f needs to suit a hold-up horse who needs time to wind up.
runners_data.comment: Medieval Night showed strong placed form two starts back and has run over today's trip, with a quick nine-day turnaround suggesting he is fit and ready; the main risk is a trainer without a winner in 23 attempts over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Marambo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push forward and challenge, she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on this flat 7f Laytown strip. The field behind her is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Roman Harry, I'm Spartacus, Movin And Groovin, Chavajod, Saith Seren, Barretstown, and Amanirenas are all true hold-up horses, though several are mapped to midfield simply because the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear. Reponse Finale, Perfect Judgement, and Medieval Night are the principal closers with genuine hold-up credentials and the form to matter late, while Brains is likely to settle just off Marambo in a small prominent group. With the pace controlled and not pressured, the race sets up as a test of late acceleration rather than stamina, and the runner positioned best to peel from midfield or the rear with a clean run will have a decisive edge — this shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can find a clear passage in the final two furlongs and finish with purpose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Marambo Dictates, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Marambo holds a comfortable lead at a honest but uncontested tempo and the race develops into a straight-line sprint for home.
scenarios.body: Marambo sets the fractions from the front unopposed, with the pack strung out behind, and the hold-up horses who find daylight earliest in the final two furlongs deliver their challenges with maximum momentum; the controlled pace keeps energy in the field and rewards those with a sharp finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Wide, Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the backmarkers, forced wide into the straight, produce a wall of late finishers that swamps any mid-race mover.
scenarios.body: The slow early tempo means energy is conserved throughout and a late surge from hold-up runners who find racing room wide becomes the dominant narrative; horses with strong sim-going records on turf and good form over this distance are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pinch It
scenarios.trigger: If Brains tracks Marambo closely, the pair quicken turning for home, and the hold-up horses fail to reel them in in time.
scenarios.body: With a small prominent group having stolen a few lengths on the closers through the final quarter-mile, the hold-up field finds the deficit too great to bridge and a clean jump from Marambo or Brains seals it; this is less likely given Marambo's poor recent form and Brains' modest sim-going record, but possible if the pace is perfectly judged.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Nightmare, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up group causes interference entering the straight, gifting a clear-run horse an advantage that others cannot match.
scenarios.body: With so many horses genuinely held up and compressing into the same section of track, at least one serious closer is baulked or checked, and the horse who avoids trouble entirely profits from the disorder; this scenario particularly benefits runners drawn or ridden widest with the clearest view of the straight.

watchPoints.text: Reponse Finale — in-form hold-up horse with two recent wins and a positive sim-going record; watch whether she secures a clear run into the straight, as a clean passage makes her the most dangerous closer in the race.

Marambo — as the lone front-runner her recent form is alarming (10-12-13) and a STYLE_FIT of 0.94 means she is essentially out of role; if she shows any sign of capitulating before the final furlong, the race opens up dramatically for the closers.

Amanirenas — the missing jockey detail is a genuine concern that should be resolved before the off; her going profile is actually strong (13/15 sim-going runs), but without a named rider the stable confidence angle cannot be read.

Traffic risk in the straight — with six to seven genuine hold-up horses all converging from behind, the final two furlongs at Laytown's tight beach track could produce significant bunching; horses drawn or positioned widest are most likely to find a clean run.

Medieval Night and Perfect Judgement — both are unraced over 7f in recent form and are stepping down from 8-10f trips; watch in-running whether either travels with enough pace to make a hold-up move over the shorter distance rather than arriving too late.

races.name: Money Back Daily Specials With Tote.ie (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form reads poorly (two 9ths and a 13th at 6f on good), with no win or place at today's track or in similar-going conditions over five attempts; dependent on a pace that this race is unlikely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Valiant Force nonetheless ranks highest of the 13 runners on our ratings and has run over today's trip, giving connections reason for hope; he carries 169 lb from stall three and, fresh off a 26-day break, must finally convert promise into performance.

runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Natural closer with a recent fourth at 7f on good going and a yard that is cold in the last two weeks; needs a stronger gallop than Exquisite Acclaim is likely to set, and the 38-day layoff adds a question mark.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Tolebi has nonetheless shown a degree of consistency with three fourth-place finishes in that sequence, and he has run over today's trip before; 38 days off and a stiff 168 lb are the obvious questions to answer from stall six.

runners_data.name: En Or
runners_data.note: A stayer squeezed into a 7f sprint, all five recent runs have been at 10-16f on good or soft ground, representing a sharp drop in trip that looks deeply uncomfortable regardless of the jockey booking.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning just three days ago, En Or at least has experience over today's trip and a speed rating of 84 that suggests more ability than his recent finishes imply — the concern is whether this quick turnaround leaves him short of his best.

runners_data.name: Genuine Article
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose last eight runs include no wins and only two places, all at 7-8f on good ground; a 14-day turnaround for a yard without a recent win in nine runs is not compelling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Genuine Article nevertheless holds an 87 rating that ranks him second of the 13 runners, suggesting he is better than recent efforts imply; carrying 167 lb from stall 8 having run over today's trip before, the worry is that his tendency to finish out of the frame makes trustworthiness an issue.

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer whose true rear-of-field style is displaced forward because the map is saturated with closers — racing out of role reduces his chance in a shape that will suit prominent types; showed ability when third at 9f good but that form doesn't transfer cleanly to a 7f Laytown sprint.
runners_data.comment: Glyndwr has placed third in his last five starts but remains yet to win, and 42 days off the track is a potential concern; he has run over today's trip and carries 166 lb from stall 10, leaving him with plenty to find at this level.

runners_data.name: Hygge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from seven runs on good ground and strong staying form at 16-17f — the drop to 7f is a significant query, but Gordon Elliott's T14 strike rate of 4/39 shows the yard is active and the horse's tactical speed makes it competitive if the trip is within range.
runners_data.comment: Hygge won two starts back but was unplaced last time, and with our rating of 74 ranking him near the foot of the field, he faces a stiff task under 166 lb from stall 1 despite that recent winning form to his name.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a win and three places at 6-7f on good, consistent without winning again; the five-pound claimer Mr A P Ryan takes the ride, and he fits the race shape well if the pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures and with his trainer winless from 23 runners in the last fortnight, Alfred Tennyson is a tough sell despite a win three starts back; he has run over today's trip and returns after a 14-day break, but the stable's current form makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Indigo Dream
runners_data.note: Front-foot runner with four places at 7f on good ground and form figures reading consistently without a win; Ross O'Sullivan's yard landed one runner from 13 in the last fortnight, offering a tentative trainer signal.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last six starts — most recently a runner-up last time out — Indigo Dream arrives just 29 days after that effort and has run over today's trip, with our rating of 83 marking her out as a serious threat; the risk is that she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Musical Act
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot by the redistribution process — its natural closing style is compromised in a race where a slow pace is expected; the 75-day absence and switch from Flat stayers' distances to 7f adds further concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of these on our figures, Musical Act faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip before and a 75-day freshen-up at least offers some hope of improvement.

runners_data.name: Summer Island
runners_data.note: Two wins at 7f on good going make the form credentials relevant, but as a true hold-up type forced to race closer to the pace than natural, the style fit is diluted; the 23-day turnaround is fine and Natalia Lupini's yard has a recent runner.
runners_data.comment: Summer Island has won twice in his last six starts, with a win three starts back, but back-to-back finishes of fifth and ninth since then make him hard to fancy, and our figures rank him near the foot of this field.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who sets the tempo uncontested, trained by the in-form Adrian McGuinness yard (T14: 4/30); recent runs at 7-8f on good suit today's conditions and a wire-to-wire effort at a sedate pace cannot be discounted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Exquisite Acclaim does at least bring distance experience and a quick turnaround of just eight days, though a sixth last time out and an unplaced effort three starts back are harder to ignore, leaving him a mid-pack proposition from stall 11 carrying 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Prominent type from the same McGuinness yard as the leader — if Exquisite Acclaim tows him into the race, he can sit in the perfect position to pounce; a win at 6f good last time out gives him recent course-trip form confidence.
runners_data.comment: Clonmacash arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, though his record in recent starts shows just that single victory amid several mid-field finishes, and carrying 163 lb may test his ability to build on that latest success.

runners_data.name: Barbapapa
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-hold-up performer with a win and three places at 6-7f on good or similar ground; the 50-day layoff and Henry De Bromhead's T14 figure of 4/26 suggest the horse is ready, though no jockey is listed which is a minor transparency concern.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner five starts back, Barbapapa has run over today's trip and carries 162 lb from stall 12, but that ninth and an unplaced effort in between are harder to ignore after a 50-day absence.

races.paceDynamic: Exquisite Acclaim is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead from the outset at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 7f Laytown test, with Clondmacash, Hygge, Alfred Tennyson, Indigo Dream, and Barbapapa tracking prominently behind. The pace is unlikely to be searingly fast with only one genuine leader, meaning the race will be run at a measured tempo that keeps the field compressed and curtails the advantage of horses who need a truly run race to produce their best. This setup strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the leader and pounce in the straight without needing a gap to appear from deep, with hold-up types who require a strong pace to reel in the leaders facing a structural disadvantage. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Glyndwr, Summer Island, and Musical Act are natural closers who are likely to be pushed forward out of their preferred position, diluting the value of any late-running scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Exquisite Acclaim leads at a controlled clip and the prominent squad travels smoothly within striking range throughout.
scenarios.body: Exquisite Acclaim sets a comfortable fractions and the prominent horses — Clonmacash, Hygge, and Alfred Tennyson — take up their natural positions just behind, hitting the short Laytown straight with momentum and fuel to spare. The lack of a pressing pace suits horses who can dictate their own rhythm and quicken when asked, making this a race for prominent types with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Nicks It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Exquisite Acclaim steals a march in the early stages and the prominent horses fail to press or quicken sufficiently in the straight.
scenarios.body: Exquisite Acclaim, uncontested and relaxed on a flat track, simply keeps finding through the final two furlongs while the chasing pack struggles to close the gap on a good-ground surface that rewards relaxed gallopers. Adrian McGuinness has been in solid form at the yard and the horse's recent Laytown-distance experience over 7-8f on good ground adds credence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens in the middle stages and a contested early tempo strings out the field, giving genuine hold-up horses a target.
scenarios.body: Tolebi or Valiant Force, racing wide of the pack, pick up strongly if the race is run at an honest pace and they can exploit a tiring front half; however, their dependence on a true gallop being set by a single front-runner is a significant structural risk. Summer Island's multiple wins on this trip and going are noteworthy, though she and Glyndwr are racing out of their natural rearward role here and may be further forward than ideal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the large 13-runner field causes crowding through the early stages, disrupting prominent horses and creating an unpredictable sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A field this size on the tight Laytown layout can produce shuffling and interference that scrambles running styles, elevating the chance of a horse who gets a clear unimpeded run regardless of position. Barbapapa or Alfred Tennyson, both placed repeatedly without winning on this trip, could capitalise if afforded a clean passage through a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Exquisite Acclaim leads unchallenged — if no horse pressures early, the controlled gallop could allow the leader to dictate the race in its entirety and land a front-running success.
Hygge drops sharply in trip from 16-17f to 7f — if the horse fails to settle or finds the distance too sharp, it will be a non-factor despite fitting the prominent shape well.
En Or runs over 7f having competed exclusively at 10-16f recently — monitor if the horse is in any difficulty early as this trip drop looks extreme and could lead to interference for others.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Glyndwr, Summer Island, Musical Act) will be closer to the pace than their natural style dictates — watch for any of them being caught wide or in an awkward position in the opening furlong, as that could create crowding in a 13-runner field.

Clonmacash and Exquisite Acclaim share the same trainer (Adrian McGuinness, T14: 4/30) — yard form is live and the potential for the leader to set up the race for the stablemate is a tactical angle worth monitoring.
